medium_value.description: Pin and revalidate both base_sha and head_sha before and after every files-page request. Discard accumulated pages and restart when either changes.

Scan the complete final record tree for symlinks, escaping paths, and prohibited secret classes, including inherited entries from head and the lite tree. Update the record ref with compare-and-swap against its expected previous value.

Define quarantine validation for malformed rows, duplicate or unknown test IDs, missing owners or beads, expiry boundaries, and maximum duration. Make the helper prove that each row matches the intended test.
Make file-descriptor cleanup handle an infinite or unusable RLIMIT_NOFILE hard limit explicitly, and add a subprocess test that inherits a high-numbered descriptor.
Define metering rules for streaming, cached usage, interrupted turns, retries, and refusal reruns. Persist consumed but unmetered attempts and distinguish accounting failure from zero spend.

Specify outcome, denominator, provenance, and attempt-selection rules for each refusal policy, including a second refusal, infrastructure failure on retry, and mixed outcomes. Preserve both attempts and charge both.

Define the proxy's upstream network attachment and enforce destination validation for both CONNECT and ordinary HTTP requests, including resolved-address restrictions and private, loopback, link-local, and metadata destinations.

Expand egress self-checks to test direct sandbox connections, DNS behavior, denied HTTP and CONNECT requests, allowed model calls, and denial attribution. Define batch-level versus run-level log routing and proxy cleanup.

Specify how the supervisor detects hangs and abnormal exits, holds its lock across daemonization, updates STATUS.json atomically with the runner, and distinguishes retryable failures from intentional stops and budget exhaustion.

Include project CLAUDE.md, local memory files, imports, nested instructions, and all configuration-discovery paths in the mount threat model and spike acceptance criteria. Require equivalent isolation before enabling fallback design (c).

Define clause (f) using versioned transcript parsing and explicit handling of partial reads and Grep results. Require sufficient changed-file coverage for the review, and require distinct PR versus pinned bytes in the negative-control fixture.
Define pagination termination, cross-page deduplication, and run-wide selection state. Apply max_files_per_pr across the entire PR and represent unknown omitted files separately from named omissions.

Resolve pipeline versioning after Sprint 3 harness changes. Pin the smoke and shipped measurements to a commit containing C-10, grader 1.5, and registration v2, and explicitly version subsequent drift-test removal.

Specify finding ID generation, file-path normalization, line bounds, confidence normalization, alias precedence, Unicode word counting, and an exact failure-scenario grammar. Add shared conformance fixtures for all four validators.

Define judged-recall eligibility and denominators, the exact finding–defect pair key, canonical hash inputs, timestamp tie handling, and how blind judgment is established. Include judge prompt/version provenance.
Bind external PR metadata and base/head commits to the cloned repository and validate fix commit or range relationships. Sanitize credentials and constrain URL schemes before cloning or logging.
Enforce file and byte limits during archive materialization and fix-diff retrieval, with bounded processing and cleanup. Reject unsupported archive entry types before extraction.

Replace the any-fix-diff-line leakage rule with a defined substantive-overlap check that excludes blank lines, diff headers, and common syntax. Specify leakage checks for PR metadata, incident content, labels, and generated reports.

Define license identification and provenance checks for committed trees, including conflicting declarations, third-party subdirectories, missing licenses, and the role of --licence. Prevent the flag from overriding incompatible evidence.
Specify the looks_seen registration graph's ordering and integrity rules, reject self-references and cycles, and define whether completeness of prior looks is verified or only declared.

Define sweep categories, evidence requirements, inventory snapshot checks, and retry-safe application logging. Specify the sample population, rounding, seed, and action when re-verification finds an incorrect closure.

Add a requirement-to-test acceptance matrix with measurable smoke and dry-run criteria. Make egress isolation, writer tool disabling, and mount isolation mandatory release gates with an explicit policy for quarantining those tests.

Specify degradation for absent GitHub patches, partially retained patches, buffer-limit failures, and incomplete page requests. Include reviewed byte or hunk coverage and omission reasons in the coverage record.
Publish one authoritative exit-code table per command and reconcile it with the global error categories, including scan refusals, seeder policy refusals, and reproduce.sh outcomes.

Require a mechanically enforced tool-disabled configuration for every eligible writer adapter. Remove codex-headless from the default allowlist until a test demonstrates that shell, file, network, and configured connector tools cannot execute.

Preserve all decision-relevant finding fields during enrichment, including failure_scenario, confidence, anchor_line_end, suggestion, and blocking metadata. Reject duplicate IDs and altered finding multiplicities.

Define a complete verdict decision table covering INFO, PRAISE, SPECULATION, REFRAME, voice-blocking findings, BLOCKER compatibility, missing verdicts, malformed blocks, and guard rejection. State when degradation blocks merging.

Separate immutable, approved release-candidate inputs from mutable publish progress. Define canonical digest serialization and explicit inclusion of patch bytes, notes, target commits, and planned ref updates.

Precompute the ledger commit deterministically, verify it is a descendant of merge_sha, and define phase-specific retry preconditions. Accept remote main at the already-published ledger commit when resuming.
Define how deferred ledger patches are stored, discovered, validated, and applied after main advances, including conflict handling and idempotent recovery by archive-cycle.sh.

Specify the safety guarantees retained by candidate-v1 publishing, including target verification and approval binding. Refuse legacy candidates that cannot meet those guarantees with a regeneration instruction.

Resolve which commit the pipeline pin points at. The header and §8 Sprint 2 exit say the pin is the Sprint 2 head, but Sprint 3 changes harness code that the smoke exercises (lib/sandbox-mount.sh home-scope mode, took-effect.sh clauses (e)/(f), ablation-grade.sh 1.5, Dockerfile.ablation CA/proxy defaults). Either state that the smoke records a Sprint 3 pin (and define a second pin step), or move the C-10/C-11 harness changes into the pinned version explicitly and say what the Sprint 3 smoke validates against.

Define the normalisation for the dual-typed confidence field ({high, medium, low} | number 0–1): the numeric mapping for the enum values, which representation the grader and verdict-derive.sh consume, and whether validators emit the canonical form.

Tighten judge-verdict ingestion in grader 1.5: refuse duplicate verdicts for a credited pair unless the later row carries an explicit supersedes reference (rather than silently letting the later ts win), and either refuse blind: false rows from recall_judged or report them in a separate column.

Complete the coverage record states and the degradation rule in C-1: add a partial state (or omitted reason patch_truncated) for a selected file whose patch was cut by max_diff_bytes; define 'reviewable code file' (by tier/extension) so that files omitted via exclude_patterns (fixtures, grade trees) do not set degraded: true on every PR that touches them.
Cap the omitted[] list rendered into the GitHub comment (e.g. counts per reason plus the first N paths) and keep the full list only in the summary JSON / marker.

Specify how truncateFiles enforces global limits (max_files_per_pr, tier ordering) in per-page mode while 'keeping its signature': pass an explicit running-budget/state object through the generator, and state that cross-page ranking is first-come within tier (or do a two-pass over filenames before retaining patches).

Align the exit-code semantics of every new script with §6.1 (2 = refusal before any write, 3 = degraded completion, 1 = failed step). record-branch.sh uses exit 3 for a scan hit (a refusal, nothing built) and seed-corpus-from-external.sh uses exit 1 for licence/leakage refusals and 2 for usage.
Have price_for and price_events return a non-zero exit status alongside the ERR sentinel, and state that callers check both.

Add a keep-list to the ENV_SHIM descriptor closing (e.g. LOA_KEEP_FDS) so descriptors deliberately passed to the session (secret fds, notify sockets, docker stdin/stdout redirections) survive, and document the default.

Broaden the assert_secret_keys pattern beyond (_KEY$|TOKEN|SECRET|PASSWORD) to include KEY anywhere (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID), CREDENTIAL, AUTH and PASS, and make the pattern a documented constant with its own unit vector.

Add a --supervised precondition that the user manager will outlive the login session (loginctl show-user --property=Linger is yes, or the batch is launched inside an existing lingering scope) and refuse with the repair otherwise.

Extend the C-10 executable surface and clause (e) to cover every path Claude Code loads independently of --setting-sources: the repository-root CLAUDE.md and CLAUDE.local.md, .mcp.json, .claude/rules/ (if present in the image's version), and any @-imported memory files. These must be removed from the workspace root and kept readable under pr/head/, and the Sprint 3 spike must plant a canary in each of them, not only in a hook, a skill and a .claude/CLAUDE.md line.

Disable or sinkhole DNS inside the sandbox on the internal network (e.g. --dns pointing at an unroutable address, or a resolv.conf with no nameservers) since HTTP CONNECT carries the hostname to the proxy, and add a DNS-denied case to egress-proxy.sh self-check.

Give the model registry an explicit per-provider egress_hosts[] list (auth and token-refresh hosts such as sts.amazonaws.com, auth.openai.com, the Bedrock control-plane host) instead of deriving the allowlist from endpoint URLs only; state that the proxy sidecar is attached to both the internal network and an external one; and either justify the CA env defaults in image 259 (tinyproxy CONNECT does not terminate TLS) or drop them.

Specify how the batch-level proxy denial log is attributed to runs: record the sandbox container's network address per run_id in meta at launch and have egress-proxy.sh split or tag denials by source address into each <run>/meta/egress-denied.jsonl.

Audit the framework hooks, skills and scripts for project-relative references to .claude/ (e.g. sourcing .claude/scripts/... from cwd) and resolve them through a single root variable set by the home-scope mount; have the spike plant a canary .claude/scripts/ file at the workspace root to detect any such read.
Pin the Claude Code version inside loa-ablation:259, record it in the spike result and in MANIFEST, and state that the spike must be re-run whenever the version changes.

For refusal_policy rerun-once, add an attempt field to the row, retain the refused attempt's transcript and meta, and emit a per-arm refusal_rate with a documented threshold above which the arm is flagged in the report; state the denominator rule in the SDD rather than only in README.

Replace 'refuses when any fix-diff line appears in PR.md' with a defined leakage test: compare only added/removed lines with at least N non-whitespace characters after normalising whitespace, excluding a stop-list of trivial tokens (braces, blank lines, import lines), and report the matching lines.

Specify the order of limit enforcement in the external seeder: check --max-files/--max-bytes from tree metadata (e.g. the GitHub git/trees API with recursive=1, or ls-tree before any blob fetch) before materialising base/ and head/ from a blob:none clone; and define base/ as the fix commit's parent (fix^ or the range start), not the PR base branch tip.

Before --commit-trees, run audit-secret-redaction-scan.sh (the same scanner C-4 uses) on the materialised base/ and head/ trees, detect the licence via the GitHub license API (SPDX id) rather than file text matching, and commit the upstream LICENSE/NOTICE files plus a third-party attribution row with the fixture.

Enumerate the sweep manifest category values and the action each maps to (close-done, close-obsolete, backlog, keep), require closure evidence to be a resolvable reference (commit sha, PR, or path that exists at head) validated by sweep-apply.sh, define the sample disagreement threshold that reverts a batch, and name the revert command (br reopen from inventory.jsonl).

Specify how clause (f) compares a Read/Grep tool result to a PR file. Read tool results carry line-number prefixes and may be windowed (offset/limit), and Grep returns matched lines only, so a raw sha256 of the tool result will essentially never equal the file's sha256. Define a normalisation (strip the line-number gutter, compare the reconstructed content or per-line hashes with a minimum covered-line fraction) or plant a per-trial canary token in each changed .claude/ file and detect the token in tool results.

Add to C-5: the list (or count) of the ten failing tests with a maximum number allowed into QUARANTINE.tsv at Sprint 1 exit; the concrete tripwire mechanism (plant a known violation under evals/fixtures/review-prs/ and assert each lint walk reports zero); the exact paths receiving linguist-generated -diff; and a note that -diff also hides those paths from local git diff/show.

Do not keep the v1 candidate publish path silently live. Make --publish refuse a schema_version 1 candidate with a repair message to regenerate, or require an explicit --allow-v1 flag with a logged reason.

Add a traceability table (defect / KF or FR → reproducing test file → component) and define the Sprint 3 smoke's pass criteria explicitly (clauses (a)–(f) satisfied, oracle_scan negative, grade.json produced under grader 1.5, pipeline pin recorded).

Move the branch-protection open question earlier: in Sprint 1 read the protection rules with the operator token (branches/main/protection, enforce_admins, required PRs) and record whether a direct fast-forward is permitted, instead of discovering it at the rc.8 publish.

Fill the unspecified values in C-4: the Session Log cap for notes-guard.sh rotate, behaviour when a template section header is missing (refuse vs emit empty), and pre-compact-marker.sh behaviour for an absent, unreadable or unknown .state (should be silent).
Scan only the paths that differ between the staged tree and <head> (git diff-tree --name-only <head> <tree>) rather than exporting and scanning the whole tree, and bound the export size.

Clarify 'new versions beside the record's' for C-7: if the new reproduce.sh, record_lite.py and judge_defects.py replace the same paths on main, state that cycle-132 reproduction (and --live-sample, which requires rc 0) must run from a worktree checked out at pin fbd36a0c, and add that instruction to the new REPRODUCE.md.

Make the writer-role ineligibility fallback a named degradation (exit 3, degraded_reason writer_not_eligible) consistent with the guard rejection, and have adapters self-report their enforced no-tool stance in the dispatch result so the role check verifies the actual invocation rather than the adapter name in writer_role_allowlist.

Reconcile §3.2 with §1.4: target_on_main: true appears only in the schema table, and the record manifest row lacks the scan_tree / accepted_scan fields that record-branch.sh writes into the commit message.

Make the markdown finding grammar tolerant of dash variants (—, –, -, --) as the title delimiter and specify how a title containing '. Failure:' is disambiguated (e.g. Failure: must begin a new sentence after the last period before end of bullet).

Change the --publish precondition from 'remote main equals merge_sha' to 'merge_sha is an ancestor of remote main' (git merge-base --is-ancestor) for the tag and release steps, and keep the exact-sha lease only for the ledger fast-forward push.

Define which failure reasons the supervisor retries (e.g. infrastructure_error, container exit without STATUS update) versus which it does not (metering_incomplete after a config fix, model refusals handled by refusal_policy), and record the reason class per retry.

Define the completion path for ledger_commit: deferred. After a lease failure the recorded expected_old (merge_sha) is permanently stale, so the stated 'a re-run completes a partial publish' cannot complete the ledger step. Add either a --publish --ledger-only mode that re-applies post-merge-ledger.patch onto the current remote main with a fresh lease taken at that moment, or an explicit fallback that opens a PR with the patch, and state which one archive-cycle.sh expects.

Make the candidate v2 ref_updates[].new field consistent with the digest. Either make the ledger commit deterministic (fixed GIT_AUTHOR_DATE/GIT_COMMITTER_DATE and identity taken from the candidate, so new is computable at --generate and verified at --publish), or state that new is excluded from the sealed digest and written to the publish phases record instead.

Scope the enrichment guard's provider tool-grammar check. Apply the denylist (<invoke, tool_use, function_call, tool_calls) only to the writer's output outside fenced code spans and outside finding title/failure_scenario string values, or match it structurally (top-level JSON keys / XML tags at line start) rather than as substrings.

Reconcile the severity vocabulary between C-2 and C-11. C-2's precedence rule names BLOCKER and a 'voice-blocking finding', but finding.schema.json v1 enumerates CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, PRAISE, SPECULATION, REFRAME, INFO with no BLOCKER and no blocking flag. Either add BLOCKER (or a boolean blocking field) to the schema or rewrite the precedence rule in terms of the v1 set.

Exempt non-defect severities (PRAISE, INFO, REFRAME, and arguably SPECULATION) from the failure_scenario minimum rule and the mandatory Failure: clause in the markdown grammar, and decide whether the enrichment guard treats a single finding's rule violation as a per-finding drop (recorded in a violations list) or as whole-block rejection.

Specify the mechanism by which the zod FindingsBlockSchema 'references' the JSON Schema finding.schema.json. Add a shared conformance vector set (e.g. .claude/schemas/finding.vectors/{valid,invalid}/*.json) that both the vitest suite (zod) and the bash/python validators (jq/jsonschema) must accept and reject identically, run in bats-tests.yml.

blockers.concern: --publish requires remote main to equal merge_sha before tagging or creating the release. Any later merge to main makes that precondition permanently false, so the candidate can never be published and the 'resumable publish' guarantee fails.
blockers.why_matters: A single unrelated merge between --generate and --publish deadlocks the release of the cycle, forcing a manual workaround in exactly the path the design was hardening.
blockers.recommendation: Require only that merge_sha is an ancestor of remote main for tag/release. Apply the lease (expected_old) solely to the ledger fast-forward; if main has moved, re-apply the ledger patch onto current main and push with the lease against the observed sha, or record deferred. Test both the moved-main and unmoved-main paths against a bare remote.

blockers.concern: Fallback design (c) for C-10 is described as a prompt contract plus clause (f) with 'D-3.1 amended', but under (c) the PR's project-scope hooks, skills, commands and settings would load and run in the sandbox. That is a different threat model (code execution from PR data), not a design tweak.
blockers.why_matters: If the spike fails and (c) is adopted mid-sprint by the agent alone, the review-catch trials run PR-supplied hooks with project trust accepted. Egress is proxied but the hook can still tamper with transcripts, grading inputs or took-effect evidence inside the sandbox, corrupting the measurement.
blockers.location: §1.4 C-10 Spike paragraph; §9 first row; §11.D D-3.1
blockers.recommendation: Make adoption of (c) an operator decision, not an autonomous amendment. Even under (c), strip hooks/, settings*.json and .mcp.json from the root (they are configuration, not review content) and add a took-effect clause that no project hook or MCP server executed (process list, hook log, canary). Record the threat-model change in the registration.

blockers.concern: Fallback design (c) replaces failed mount isolation with a reviewer instruction and a positive-read check.
blockers.why_matters: Neither mechanism prevents loading malicious project hooks or skills, and reading one correct PR file does not establish a safe execution environment.
blockers.recommendation: Fail closed when the isolation spike fails and use a separate sanitized review workspace with enforced execution boundaries before continuing trials.

blockers.concern: Findings that fail the new Failure-clause grammar are excluded from verdict tallies, with no explicit blocking outcome for the violations.
blockers.why_matters: A genuine HIGH or CRITICAL finding can disappear from the merge decision because of formatting rather than substantive invalidity.
blockers.recommendation: Make invalid finding output produce an indeterminate, merge-blocking result and require repair before deriving an approval.

blockers.concern: Hostname-level access to model providers is treated as the egress boundary without addressing arbitrary traffic or attacker-selected accounts on those same hosts.
blockers.why_matters: A compromised sandbox can transmit data through an allowed provider endpoint even though every hostname check passes.
blockers.recommendation: Define the supported threat model and, where data exfiltration must be prevented, use a credential-owning gateway that constrains API operations and destinations.

blockers.concern: Review degradation is recorded, but the design does not explicitly make omitted reviewable code block merge eligibility.
blockers.why_matters: A review can omit security-relevant code because of limits or truncation and still produce an approval that downstream automation treats as complete.
blockers.location: C-1 coverage record; C-2 verdict derivation; §6
blockers.recommendation: Define a mandatory merge-blocking outcome for incomplete review coverage and test every consumer against degraded approvals.

blockers.concern: Security-critical container tests can be quarantined, and smoke exit criteria require a grade without specifying acceptable isolation or correctness outcomes.
blockers.why_matters: CI and release milestones can pass while the new mount or egress boundary is unverified or failing.
blockers.location: C-5 quarantine; §7.1 integration tests; §8 Sprint 3 exit
blockers.recommendation: Make isolation, egress-denial and provenance checks mandatory release gates, disallow quarantine for those checks, and define explicit smoke pass criteria.

blockers.concern: The C-10 'executable surface' (skills/, commands/, agents/, hooks/, settings*.json) omits other PR-controlled paths that Claude Code loads or executes regardless of --setting-sources: project .mcp.json (MCP servers are spawned commands), repo-root CLAUDE.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md and .claude/rules/**. Memory files are not 'settings' and are read from the project root; project MCP config can be auto-approved when project trust is accepted, which the design does. PR-supplied content would therefore still reach the reviewer as instructions or as spawned processes.
blockers.why_matters: The whole security claim of §1.9 ('PR-supplied .claude/ content is data only') fails if any one of these paths is left at the workspace root. A malicious or accidental PR could execute a command via .mcp.json or steer the review via CLAUDE.md, defeating the review-catch measurement and the sandbox's purpose.
blockers.location: §1.4 C-10, §11.A Glossary 'Executable surface', §1.9 Security Architecture, check_mount_closed clause (e)
blockers.recommendation: Extend the executable/prompt surface to .mcp.json, CLAUDE.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md, .claude/rules/** and any *.local.* under .claude/. Remove them from the root, keep them under pr/head/, and have clause (e) assert their absence. Plant each one in the Sprint 3 spike with a canary side effect (file write) so the spike proves non-loading per mechanism, not just by transcript inspection.

blockers.concern: The HOME-scope mount excludes settings and selected executable paths but leaves project instruction content such as CLAUDE.md at the workspace root.
blockers.why_matters: Settings-source isolation alone is not established as an instruction-loading boundary, so PR-controlled text may influence the reviewer before review begins.
blockers.location: C-10 HOME-scope layout and executable-surface definition
blockers.recommendation: Explicitly enumerate and isolate every instruction-discovery surface, including nested files and imports, and require tests proving PR instructions never enter trusted startup context.

blockers.concern: The codex-headless writer is classified as having no tools based on a read-only sandbox and omission of forwarded tools, without establishing that its native tools are disabled.
blockers.why_matters: A writer processing adversarial review content could still read sensitive files or invoke available capabilities before its output reaches the enrichment guard.
blockers.recommendation: Require an explicit capability restriction that disables native tools, isolate writer credentials and filesystem access, and test attempted tool calls for every eligible adapter.

blockers.concern: The enrichment guard compares finding identity, location and severity but does not preserve failure scenarios, confidence, suggestions or the meaning of surrounding prose.
blockers.why_matters: The writer can preserve the compared tuples while changing the evidence, inventing unsafe remediation or presenting a contradictory human-facing conclusion.
blockers.recommendation: Preserve canonical findings unchanged and render their verdict deterministically; restrict enrichment to clearly separated commentary that cannot replace finding content.

blockers.concern: The paged fetch checks head SHA before each page but specifies no final consistency check and does not revalidate base SHA.
blockers.why_matters: A PR update during the final request or a base-branch change can yield patches that do not correspond to the recorded base/head pair.
blockers.recommendation: Validate both base and head after fetching, discard inconsistent results, and obtain immutable comparison data where possible.

blockers.concern: The pipeline is pinned at the Sprint 2 head even though Sprint 3 changes the mount, took-effect checks, grader and registration behavior.
blockers.why_matters: The smoke can execute an older implementation or record provenance that does not identify the code actually tested.
blockers.recommendation: Create and record a new immutable pipeline pin after all Sprint 3 measurement changes, and assert that the smoke executes that exact tree.

blockers.concern: The proxy design validates hostnames but does not specify destination-address validation, CONNECT port restrictions or DNS-rebinding handling.
blockers.why_matters: An allowed hostname resolving to a private or link-local address, or a CONNECT request to an unintended port, can undermine the intended egress boundary.
blockers.recommendation: Validate every resolved destination against prohibited address ranges, constrain ports, bind validation to the actual connection, and test alternate hostname encodings and DNS changes.

blockers.concern: The release's initial remote-main equality check conflicts with recovery after a successful ledger push, when main has already advanced beyond merge_sha.
blockers.why_matters: A crash after the push but before phase recording can make the promised resumable publish refuse its own completed state.
blockers.recommendation: Define a recovery state machine that accepts either the original merge or the verified ledger result and reconciles remote state before applying initial preconditions.

blockers.concern: verdict-derive.sh tallies only bullets whose Failure: clause passes the ≥12-word/when-then rule and 'reports the others as violations'. A CRITICAL or HIGH bullet that lacks or malforms its Failure clause is therefore excluded from the blocking tally, and the derived verdict can be APPROVE.
blockers.why_matters: This is a fail-open path in a merge gate, contradicting the SDD's own principle that every value feeding a decision fails closed. Any model that forgets the clause (or a template regression) silently removes blocking findings from the verdict.
blockers.location: §1.4 C-11 verdict-derive.sh; §5.2 new violation class finding-without-failure-clause
blockers.recommendation: Treat a blocking-severity bullet with a missing or invalid Failure clause as still blocking (count it and emit the violation), or force verdict UNKNOWN with mergeBlocked: true when any such bullet exists. Add a red test: one malformed CRITICAL bullet must not yield APPROVE.
